title: Enforce Admin Panel Password Protection & Session Lock

requirements.text: Rewrite the AdminGuard component so that on every page load (including refresh and browser reopen) it synchronously checks for a valid admin session in localStorage before rendering any admin content. If no valid session exists, immediately redirect to /login. The session must have a timestamp-based expiry (24 hours by default). Remove any logic that allows bypassing the session check.

quotes: Rewrite the Admin Panel logic so that it MUST check for an active session on every single page load. If no user is logged in, redirect them instantly to the /login page.

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating directly to /admin without a session redirects to /login immediately.
Refreshing the browser on any admin page without a session redirects to /login.
A valid session allows access to /admin and all sub-pages.
An expired session (older than 24 hours) is treated as no session and redirects to /login.

requirements.text: Re-enable the hardcoded password check on the admin login page. The login form must validate the entered password against the stored admin credential before creating a session. If the password is incorrect, show an error message and do not create a session. Do not allow the admin panel to be accessed without successful password entry.

quotes: Re-enable the password requirement for the Admin Panel. Use the same password I set before (or let me set a new one now). No one should access /admin without entering the correct credentials.

acceptanceCriteria: Submitting a wrong password shows an error and does not start a session.
Submitting the correct password creates a session and redirects to /admin.
The login page is publicly accessible at /login.

requirements.text: Implement a 'Remember Me' checkbox on the admin login page. When checked, persist the session in localStorage with a 7-day expiry (instead of session-only). When unchecked, clear the session on browser close by using sessionStorage so that reopening the browser requires re-authentication. If 'Remember Me' is not checked, the session must not survive a browser restart.

quotes: Ensure that even if someone refreshes the page or reopens the browser, they are asked for a password again unless they have a valid 'Remember Me' cookie.

acceptanceCriteria: With 'Remember Me' checked, reopening the browser keeps the admin session active for up to 7 days.
Without 'Remember Me', reopening the browser clears the session and requires re-login.
Refreshing the page with 'Remember Me' active does not log the user out.
A logout button clears the session regardless of Remember Me setting.

requirements.text: Wrap ALL admin routes — including /admin, /admin/settings, /admin/qr, /admin/billing, and any other /admin/* sub-routes — with the AdminGuard component so that none of them are publicly accessible. No admin page or sub-page should render any content before the session check passes.

quotes: Ensure that the new 'Settings' and 'QR' pages are also behind this password wall. Do not allow any part of the Admin Panel to be public.

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /admin/settings without a session redirects to /login.
Navigating to /admin/qr without a session redirects to /login.
Navigating to /admin/billing without a session redirects to /login.
All /admin/* routes are covered by AdminGuard — no admin route is accessible without authentication.

constraints: Do not modify any files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui.
The existing AdminGuard component at frontend/src/components/AdminGuard.tsx must be rewritten in place, not replaced with a new file.
Do not remove or alter Internet Identity (ICP) authentication logic — the admin password check is a separate layer on top of it.
The admin password must remain hardcoded in the frontend (same approach as existing AdminGuard) unless the user provides a new password.
nonGoals: Activating Home Page features (Wallet, Search, My Orders) — that is a separate request.
Storing admin credentials in the backend canister.
Adding multi-user admin accounts or role management.
Implementing OAuth or third-party authentication for the admin panel.
